Re-solving from the constraints gives the same schedule as before. The arrangement is unique.

**Key deductions:**
- Cara is two slots after Ivo (exactly one person between them), and Ivo is after Dev, so Dev ≤ 6.
- Ben, Elif, and Gus occupy three consecutive slots in the order Ben, Elif, Gus.
- Dev can't be 3 or 4, which rules out those cases. Dev can't be 6 or later, because Ivo and Cara wouldn't fit. So Dev = 5, Ann = 6, Ivo = 7, Cara = 9.
- Two options remain for Ben/Elif/Gus. Ben in slot 1 puts Finn at 4 and breaks "Ann and Finn at least three apart." Ben in slot 2 works.

**Checked against all 17 constraints:** Finn 1 < Dev 5; Ben 2 and Gus 4 have one person between; Dev 5 < Ivo 7; Cara 9 and Finn 1 are 8 apart; Cara 9 and Ivo 7 have one person between; Ann 6 and Cara 9 are 3 apart; Elif 3 < Ann 6; Ivo 7 < Cara 9; Ben 2 < Gus 4; Cara 9 and Elif 3 are 6 apart; Ben 2 < Dev 5; Elif 3 < Cara 9; Gus 4 is immediately after Elif 3; Ann 6 < Hana 8; Ann 6 and Finn 1 are 5 apart; Ann 6 is immediately after Dev 5; Ben 2 < Ivo 7. All hold.

**Correction to the shared note:** "Ann before Hana forces Hana into the last slot" is wrong. Ann < Hana only requires Hana to come after slot 6. In this schedule Hana is in slot 8 and Cara is in slot 9. The schedule is right, but that note's reasoning isn't.
